This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2022.   If you are interested in the game and it's before February 1st, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.

A keyboard-based hacking game.

Midnight Protocol calls itself a tactical RPG, though I disagree. Midnight Protocol is a strange keyboard-based game that completely removes the mouse from the game. It also is a hacking simulator where players have to breach networks that are more similar to Uplink or Hacknet. Though controlling the entire experience through just a command line makes for a very interesting experience. 

I’m a little shocked to announce this isn’t made by Zachtronics, and yet still really feels like a Zachtronics style game. The entire game gives the player the power to breach networks and then adds moral choices such as robbing random people and earning profits as a black hat hacker, or trying to remain noble as a white hat hacker. There’s a strong narrative as well, which is intriguing. 

Pick this up if you think you’d be willing to play a keyboard-based command-line game. The game is interesting and unique as you’ll see but if you aren’t intrigued by a game that only allows the player to use the keyboards, this one probably won’t be for you. It’s a special game, yet I adore this one. 

If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel: https://youtu.be/j3gs3-4WiQI

review_text_raw:
Midnight protocol is a brilliant game.

The hacking is presented through awesome animations and graphics. The game would've been completely different without them. The enemies, the programs, the firewalls. All of them have their own models and animations. The graphics is one of the pillars that sets Midnight Protocol apart from others.

The mechanics themselves are solid - you presented with a myriad of ways to create your own playstyle. Full stealth, full damage, bypass and damage, randomness, certainty. There are so many viable combinations that everyone will find something that fits them. Ah, and also, you interact with the game only through keyboard, which adds to the atmosphere.

The plot is cool by itself, and I will eat my keyboard if you are able to predict all the twists.

The final piece - the music. It is wonderful. I go to sleep with one of the themes playing in my head.
The music sets the atmosphere for different situations. 
Are you okay or about to be caught? Are you in the menu or in the battle? Is that a boss battle? There are not many tracks, but all of them are awesome.

Even in its full price, the game is worth it.
It's a unique experience.

The fact that less than 40% of players finish the tutorial (based on steam achievement numbers) speaks volumes.

Devs, when you incorporate a help function into your game that only displays half the commands available, you need to rethink your life.

After the rather patronising tutorial, the difficulty spikes so hard you essentially have to plan out every single step before you do anything. Moving around is tedious. Having to manually end each turn is tedious. There is no undo, no way to reload from a save point, you can see everything collapsing and you can't do anything about it.

And of course the game throws a bunch of upgrades at you really early on, that you can't use because you only get a few slots and they are all taken up with the basic stuff you have to have. I have no idea why game devs think it is interesting or clever to throw stuff like this so early in the game as though we all have ADD and need new shiny stuff to stay interested, only to troll us by making them impossible to use.

Another promising indie game ruined because it trolls its players hard and hasn't done basic playtesting.

Here's to hoping this franchise will prosper, and a strong recommendation for all hacking game fans who may be turned off by annoying timers elsewhere.

Let's start with the positives. The visuals are very good, very "hackery" and just very pleasing to look at. It's also keyboard only, which further enhances the immersion.

And this is about it when it comes to the positives.

It's almost fundamentally not a hacking game. You could easily swap out all of the "commands" for just fantasy spells. You're not breaking into systems to gather information, to gather passwords to use on other networks (i.e. puzzle solving). Each "mission" is fundamentally independent. You're there to get money (or complete objectives for the story) and then leave.

There's also the weird RNG aspect of the game. Your "attacks" against "firewalls" can "crit". Not to mention, how many actions waste your action points, which is also complemented by how few turns you actually from being caught.

The developer has a solid foundation to creating an interesting hacking game. But if they're going to do a RNG/RPG turn-based game, then stick to fantasy/sci-fi instead.

review_text_raw:
Midnight Protocol is a great way to relax if you want to get away from realism and just enjoy the style.
If I wanted realism, I'd go to HackTheBox or TryHackMe and actually mess around with real-world stuff.  But if I want enough of an abstraction of the activity of hacking, Midnight Protocol gives me that.
One drawback is that I find the soundtrack to be a bit dour, but it's really a small criticism.  It's a great soundtrack, I just think that other hacking games have a more "upbeat" feel to them, and it would be the perfect complement.  There's not enough energy and tension in the music, but this is a really forgivable shortcoming.
I also enjoy the classic names given to the hacking tools, it gives it a really "gamey" feel that reminds me of the card game "Android: Netrunner".  I'm not here for deep technical stuff, I just want enough there to remind me of hacking without it actually being hacking.  If my hacking tool is an actual flurry of swords breaking down an actual wall, that's fine with me.
If you want realism, get a subscription or a free account on TryHackMe or HackTheBox.  But if you want a nice little hacking game that's pretty fun that gives you plenty of strategic moments, play this game.

If my hacking tool is an actual flurry of swords breaking down an actual wall, that's fine with me. If you want realism, get a subscription or a free account on TryHackMe or HackTheBox. But if you want a nice little hacking game that's pretty fun that gives you plenty of strategic moments, play this game.

I have been playing this game for some time and I always liked how immersive the game is.
I was there when it got playtested on G.Round, I have made videos on the game and even streamed it.
And now I come with something new! 

I recently got a Steamdeck (256GB version), and I am currently testing out how well games work on the SteamDeck etc.
So the following points will be about Midnight on the StreamDeck!

[h1] The Immersion I talked about.. [/h1]
The immersion is a bit gone on the Steam Deck as it's only partially playable, as the game is fully playable with keyboard. For the Steam Deck that means that you have to press the Steam button + the X button at the same time to open the keyboard. The immersion of hacking was a bit gone and I grew more tired of constantly having to do the button combinations and then press a letter on the keyboard and continue, sometimes having to do the same action 4 times in a row just to start a mission. I felt more like a developer than hacker doing this.
After a while you do get used to it, but it takes away some of the joy.

[h1] The Good [/h1]
The graphics defintly do not go to waste on the SteamDeck, it's fun to carry a 'puzzle'like game as Midnight Protocol with you and being able to play it where you go, the performance worked very well and I didn't experience any lag on the Deck. The story is very very good and Midnight Protocol is really one of a kind, so being able to travel and show this game easily to friends is a big plus. 

[h1] The Nuisance [/h1] 
For some reasons some buttons were linked to numbers (Pressing B = typing E in chat, pressing Y = Typing F in chat and pressing X = typing R in chat). Due to the x button being linked to typing R in chat, you would always type a R when opening the keyboard in the game. This way I often had to either backspace before typing firstly or had to retype certain commands as it stated rend or rmove wasn't a command.

Overall a great game and if you are willing to force yourself through that tedious keyboard command for the SteamDeck, definitely try it out on there if you have one! For the PC, it's such an immersive game, it really makes you feel like you are the hacker by having to type in the commands, typing emails and much more.

This game is special one! I've been looking so long for something
that could scratch my itch from playing Netrunner, since it became
out of print at 2017, specially when my LGS (and most of them)
keep supporting heavily mtg and Pokémon TCG..

When I play Midnight Protocol, I feel like I'm the Runner, but in a
realistic way, like "real-life" runner, when you have tools at your
hand whenever you need, and your work is to manage them wisely.
I'm still at the beginning, but maybe it would be awesome if you can
be the "Corp", in other words, a mode that you can hunt the runner
like the Virtual SysCon "Playground" environments AI.

I give this a wholehearted recommendation, and specially the game
that inspired the designers, that is, Android Netrunner (or Netrunner)
through jinteki online platform.
Congratulations to developers on bringing their vision of that into
Midnight Protocol, outstanding work!

Stopped having fun after 2 hours and do not intend to continue :( Game seems okay but I could not figure out which tools to use correctly to finish levels. You can cheat the system by keep restarting but I do not find that approach fun. I try to do my best first try every level and roll with the punches but like I said I could not figure out a good way to do it. 

You can bring 5 tools with you to every level, and there is a trace counter increasing at every step where the maximum trace results in a failure. Then you need to bring an item called cloak to decrease the probability of gaining trace, then because you need to use cloak you cannot use some other items so they are gone. If there are blockers in your way you need the sniffer to find them and dagger to destroy them while hoping cloak does its work. This is already 3 out of 5 items fixed for you. I don't know, I do not get it and I do not find it fun so I do not recommend the game.
